content.title: Suspected or confirmed INFECTION plus signs of organ dysfunction
items: Cardiovascular: tachycardia, hypotension, prolonged cap refill >3s, mottled skin
Respiratory: tachypnea, increased WOB, new O₂ requirement
Labs: lactate >2, base deficit >5, INR >2, creatinine elevated, platelets <100k

content.caption: Phoenix Sepsis Score ≥2 with suspected infection = Sepsis

node.label: TIME ZERO — Start Bundle
node.description: Clock starts. Draw cultures. Do NOT delay antibiotics.

rows: GBS, E. coli, S. pneumoniae, HSV
S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae

content.title: Consider additional coverage
items: HSV risk (<28d, vesicles, seizures, elevated LFTs): Acyclovir 20 mg/kg q8h
Abdominal source: Add Metronidazole 10 mg/kg (max 500 mg)

content.notes: Check glucose — if <60 mg/dL, give D10W 2 mL/kg. Check lactate.

node.label: Fluid Resuscitation
node.description: 10-20 mL/kg NS boluses, reassess after each

content.title: Rapid fluid administration
items: Watch for fluid overload: hepatomegaly, new rales, worsening respiratory distress

node.label: Fluid-Responsive Sepsis
node.description: Continue monitoring, reassess q15 min, recheck lactate at 2-4 hr

rows: Cool extremities, delayed cap refill, narrow pulse pressure
Bounding pulses, flash cap refill, wide pulse pressure
content.caption: Peripheral vasopressors are ACCEPTABLE when central access not yet obtained

content.title: Catecholamine-resistant shock
items: Consider hydrocortisone 1-2 mg/kg IV (max 100 mg) for catecholamine-resistant shock
Titrate vasopressors to MAP and perfusion targets
Activate transfer to PICU EARLY — do not wait for full stabilization
Reassess every 5 minutes during active resuscitation

blocks.text: Pediatric sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in children worldwide. The first hour of recognition and treatment is the most critical window. The 2024 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines and 2024 Phoenix Sepsis criteria provide an updated, evidence-based framework for recognition and management.
Time to antibiotics is the single most impactful intervention. Every hour of delay in antibiotics increases mortality. Target: IV antibiotics within 30 minutes of sepsis recognition.

The Phoenix Sepsis Score provides international consensus criteria for pediatric sepsis. It evaluates four organ systems: respiratory, cardiovascular, coagulation, and neurological. A score ≥2 in the setting of suspected infection defines sepsis. Septic shock is defined as sepsis with cardiovascular dysfunction requiring vasoactive medication or having lactate >5 mmol/L.

blocks.title: Rural ED Warning
blocks.body: In the rural ED, do NOT wait for lab results to begin treatment. Clinical suspicion of sepsis should trigger the bundle immediately. Labs confirm but should never delay intervention.

blocks.text: Isotonic crystalloid (normal saline or lactated Ringer's) is given in 10-20 mL/kg boluses over 5-10 minutes. Reassess perfusion after EACH bolus — do not give standing orders for multiple boluses without reassessment. The maximum recommended volume in the first hour is 40-60 mL/kg, though this may be exceeded if the patient continues to respond.
Balanced crystalloids (LR) may be preferred over NS for large-volume resuscitation to reduce hyperchloremic acidosis.
For fluid-refractory shock (persistent hypotension or poor perfusion after 40-60 mL/kg), vasopressor support is indicated. The choice of agent depends on the clinical phenotype of shock.

Peripheral vasopressors are acceptable in the emergency setting when central venous access has not yet been established. Epinephrine and norepinephrine can be safely administered through a well-functioning peripheral IV with site checks every 15 minutes.
